findings.issue: writeStockOrCompensate zeroes stock on every RuntimeException, including a ValidationException where no write can have committed (quantity < 0 checked before the call, or an inventory 400/403). With quantity < 0 and a valid warehouse, the zeroing PUT creates a 0-quantity row for an offer that is about to be discarded. That row is an orphan that shows in GET /api/seller/stock, which is the caveat the design wanted to limit to the timeout case. Each 400 also costs an extra inventory call.
findings.fix: Only zero when the failure is not a ValidationException, i.e. the stock state is unknown (5xx, timeout or fallback). Discard and rethrow in every case.

findings.issue: offerService.syncPrices runs inside writeStock after a successful putStock. If syncPrices throws, the compensation zeroes stock that was written correctly, discards the offer, and rethrows the raw exception, so the client gets a 500, not the documented 400/503.
findings.fix: Decide whether a syncPrices failure should undo the create. If it should not, move syncPrices out of the compensated block. If it should, map the failure to 503 and add a short test.

findings.issue: Reported deviation: updateOffer (and bulk update-only rows) now turn an inventory 5xx, timeout or open circuit into a 503, but the offer update has already committed. The client sees 503 while the price and other changes are live. This is the same partial-commit behaviour as before, and the status code is now more accurate, but the contract change is not documented yet.
findings.fix: In slice 2 (T9), add to docs/reference/endpoints.md that PUT offer can return 503 after the offer fields have been saved and only the stock write failed, so a retry is safe.

findings.issue: nullQuantityCreatesOfferWithoutStock stubs view.getAvailableQuantity() to 0 and then asserts 0, so it cannot prove the 'zero available' half of AC-9. Only the no-stock-call and no-discard checks carry weight. discardFailureStillRethrowsOriginal also does not assert the OFFER_STOCKLESS log.
findings.fix: Assert zero available against the real OfferService.quantity: seller offer with an empty row list gives 0 (point to an existing OfferService test or add one). Optionally capture the log line.

findings.issue: Timeout ordering: when the original PUT timed out on the client but is still running in inventory, the zeroing PUT can commit first, and the late write then leaves N units on the discarded offer. A concurrent retry can also get 409 while the first request is still compensating, and the offer is then deleted. Neither is reachable for a reservation once slice 2's fail-closed lands, but the gap is not documented.
findings.fix: Add both cases to the orphan-row caveat in the T9 docs and the PR description. No code change needed in this slice.

findings.issue: zeroStock builds the same InventoryDto.StockWrite as writeStock, differing only in quantity.
findings.fix: Extract a private stockWrite(o, warehouseCode, qty) helper used by both.

findings.issue: A SKU is added to `seen` before the row is processed, so if the first occurrence fails validation, a later corrected row with the same SKU is reported as a duplicate. This matches AC-10's wording but may surprise sellers.
findings.fix: Optional: say in the docs that the first occurrence wins even when it errors.

findings.issue: If product-service ever returns an offer with an offerId but a null sellerId, the line defaults to PLATFORM_SELLER. Once slice 2 lands, that would re-open the platform fallback for the line (the design's trust risk).
findings.fix: Optional: send null sellerId when offerId != null and offer.sellerId() == null, so inventory's owner lookup decides. Or leave it and note it in the design risk.

findings.issue: Fully qualified org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor and Tuple names in the tests, and unrelated Spotless reformatting in OrderService.cartFingerprint and DependencyBreakerCapabilityTest, add diff noise.
findings.fix: Use imports. The reformatting is acceptable as Spotless output.

summary: Slice 1 does what T1-T4 ask. Offer create compensation: a stock-write failure on a newly created offer does a best-effort zeroing PUT (failure only logged), then discards the offer (OfferService.discard: delete, flush, syncPrices) or deletes the product, then rethrows. 400/403 stay a ValidationException and 5xx, timeout and the open-circuit IllegalStateException become UpstreamUnavailableException (503). A failed undo logs OFFER_STOCKLESS. This meets CTO condition 1 and AC-8. createProduct and bulk choose the right undo: catalog.delete when the row created the product, discard when it created only the offer, nothing when it only updated. That meets AC-11. Bulk de-dup on trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT) gives 'duplicate sku in file' with correct row numbers and a 200, meeting AC-10. The product listener guard returns before applyInventorySignal when offerId != null. The production value deserializer (spring-kafka JsonDeserializer, set in application.yml) is the one the unknown-field test uses, so the test reflects production. order-service maps the line's sellerId (PLATFORM by default, else the offer's seller) through StockLine and Item. The old Item constructors are kept and the field is additive. Inventory's tolerance of the new field is verified in slice 2 (T8). Engineer's deviations: updateOffer returning 503 with no compensation is acceptable because update is not a create (document it, minor). Covering only the quantity-given path in the createProduct 503 test is acceptable because a null quantity is coerced to 0 and takes the same path. The DependencyBreakerCapabilityTest cast is a test-only fix for an ambiguous lambda and is fine. The tests would catch regressions: removing de-dup, compensation, zeroing, the 503 mapping or the listener guard each fails a test. The exception is the AC-9 zero-available assertion, which is tautological. AC-9 needs slice 2's reserve rejection to be fully met, and AC-1 to AC-7 are slice 2. No duplicated platform code was found: no existing offer-delete method exists, and ProductCatalogService.delete is reused. No blocker or major findings.
